summary: Riverton Transit announced a six-month pilot with ten electric buses on routes 4 and 8, starting October 1. The agency will keep fares and schedules unchanged and measure energy use and reliability before deciding whether to expand.

Riverton completed four charging stations at its central bus depot for the planned electric bus pilot. A state grant paid for the chargers. The transit agency said staff training and final safety checks must finish before service starts.

Riverton drivers began training for ten electric buses scheduled to enter service in October. Union representatives welcomed quieter vehicles but asked the agency to publish battery performance data during cold weather. No winter performance results are available yet.

Riverton Transit said it would publish monthly reliability and energy-use reports during its electric bus trial. Officials said any decision to buy more buses would depend on the trial results and future funding; no expansion has been approved.
